content.text: The verifier's substantive review confirms the classification: the only failed item is the deterministic "audit frequency limited" check, which cannot pass where no audit clause exists, and the reviewer expressly notes that is expected noise. No redline is appropriate for a compliant finding. I'll re-submit with the rationale tightened to address that check head-on.

input.quote: Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services in a timely and effective manner.
input.rationale: No audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right exercisable against the Customer (AP) exists anywhere in this Agreement. Full-text searches for "audit", "records", "inspect" and "verif" return no hits, and a paragraph-by-paragraph read of the single section confirms it: the Fees and Payment provision (§5, p0023) creates no examination or true-up right, and the only access-related obligation on AP (§1, p0001) is cooperation so Kubient can deliver the Services — not a right to examine AP's books, usage or systems. Because Kubient holds no audit right at all, there is no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access term to constrain, and the position is at least as favourable to us as the preferred standard (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, Vendor cost, no system access). Compliant is therefore the correct classification rather than "missing", which would perversely require inserting an audit obligation against ourselves. The deterministic "audit frequency limited" check necessarily fails where no audit clause exists; that is expected noise and does not indicate a gap to repair. No redline is warranted. Parked for the deal team and not double-flagged here: Impressions are measured solely "as measured by Kubient" (p0009) and revenue share runs through the Exhibits with no AP-side reporting or verification right — an audit right running in our favour over Kubient's reporting would benefit us and belongs under the reporting/revenue-verification rule.
